evidence_layer: synthetic memory oracle: the original ARM bytes of THREE bodies (0x1abd9c CRoom::UpdateActive, 0x1d30a4 UpdateActiveLists, 0x1d3074 ProcessActivateDeactveLists) executed over the image's own .bss cells, with the bl chain landing in the next body's original bytes and every unrecovered callee stubbed identically on both arms; NOT device execution

vfp_compare_semantics.reading: bls is taken only for an ORDERED cur <= new; an unordered compare walks on like "greater" does, so a NaN depth sinks to the TAIL and the C model is `a <= b`, not `!(a > b)`

real_link.ProcessActivateDeactveLists@0x1d3074: both arms: the judge arm runs its bytes because F2 bls to it, the claim arm runs the C translation
real_link.CRoom::UpdateActive@0x1abd9c: both arms: reached through F3, so the queue-count -> chain-rewrite link is real on both sides

heap_model.note: the fill byte is asserted, not incidental: bytes no body writes must still compare equal across the two arms

covered: F1: both walk directions (dormant TAIL via +0x178, active TAIL via +0x178); all four branch pairs; the two unlink field sets (0x8c/0x90 and 0x80/0x84); the three active-chain insert flavours (empty / in-front-of-a-node / tail-append) including the head republish at 0x1abf38; the two dormant-chain inserts (empty and head); the depth-descending order with `bls` == <= OR unordered (equal depth, NaN on either side); the SNAPSHOT +0x184 as the sort key and its refresh at insert time; the word copy of +0x180 into +0x184 on the empty-chain path; both counters including their wrap behaviour; both bls with the CObjectGM* read out of inst+0x80 and the instance in r1

F2: the three queue tests in machine order, `cmp/bne` as a NON-ZERO (not positive) test -- counts -1 and 0x80000000 both flush; the three fall-through edges; handler A cleared count and the stub-cleared B/C counts; the profile Push(6,7)/Pop pair on the same object and the exit RE-READING the switch byte (a handler that clears it yields Push without Pop); the GROW model through the shared bump arena
F3: the Run_Room singleton hop (not the caller's r0), the queue count clear, and the r0 pass-through of UpdateActive's result
not_covered: the semantics of every stubbed callee: a green run says the chain passes the right ARGUMENTS to them and passes their r0 through, nothing more

what the two real handlers do with their queue: the stub clears the count and honours the AUX knob, and that is a MODEL.  The array growth of a queue container therefore is not graded as the original's behaviour -- only the harness's GROW model is, and only for the case shapes staged here
inst+0x69 has no write point in F1: WHICH body sets or clears the deactivated flag (and when) is not in this arm, so "deactivate then reactivate across frames" is staged as input, never produced
the class identity of the CProfiler object and what (6,7) mean beyond being Push's two arguments
device behaviour: this is a synthetic-memory oracle over the original bytes, not execution on a phone
observability: every case compares the returned word (r0 residue included), every word of every staged region (12 regions, pointers normalised to region tokens) and every allocated block, so a store the translation forgot and a store it invented both show up

the call log records each stub call in order with the arguments the body passed: the CObjectGM* (read out of inst+0x80 by the body, not by the harness) and the instance pointer (which the body never materialises explicitly -- it relies on r1 still holding it)
the stubs return magic constants, so "does this body return its callee's r0" is graded, not assumed

staging_geometry.shared: one write program interpreted by both arms; only the region bases differ (the judge arm uses the image's own .bss cells for Q/C/B/W/F/S, the claim arm its own globals)

findings: CRoom::UpdateActive sorts the ACTIVE chain by the SNAPSHOT at inst+0x184, never by the live depth at +0x180, and it refreshes that snapshot on every insert (0x1abe40 / 0x1abf48 / 0x1abf5c).  A depth change therefore does NOT reorder the chain: the instance has to leave (deactivate) and come back for the order to follow its new depth.  Case F1-l is the one that separates the two keys.

CARD DRIFT, measured: the walk's `vcmpe.f32` + `bls` is an ORDERED <= only.  VCMP leaves FPSCR = 0110 (equal), 0010 (greater), 1000 (less) and 0011 on UNORDERED -- C=1, Z=0 -- so `ls` (C == 0 || Z == 1) is FALSE for a NaN on either side and the walk steps past it like it steps past a greater node.  A NaN depth therefore sinks to the TAIL, it does not jump to the head (cases F1-m, F1-n).  The C model is `a <= b`, NOT `!(a > b)`: the latter is true for NaN and is exactly the "bls == <= or unordered" gloss this line carried before the differential disagreed with it.  Note the same idiom sits at CRoom::AddInstance 0x1ab680 in c/room_add, whose translation uses `!(a > b)` and whose case set has no NaN depth, so that arm cannot see this.

both counters are read-modify-write with NO clamp and NO sign test: a dormant count of 0 minus one move becomes 0xffffffff (F1-p), and an active count of 0xffffffff plus one wraps to 0 (F1-t).  The counts are therefore only trustworthy if the chains and the counters were consistent to begin with, which nothing in these 116 instructions checks.

the two bls take the CObjectGM* out of inst+0x80 in r0 and rely on r1 STILL holding the instance -- no instruction between 0x1abe00 and 0x1abe54 writes r1.  The C++ signature (CObjectGM::AddInstance(CInstance*)) agrees, so the body is passing (this = *(inst+0x80), inst) and nothing else.

UpdateActiveLists tests `cmp/bne`, i.e. NON-ZERO, not positive: a queue count of -1 or 0x80000000 flushes the queue exactly like +1 (F2-g, F2-h, F2-o).  `if (count > 0)` would silently skip a queue whose count underflowed.

the profile switch byte 0x757e7c is read TWICE -- at entry (0x1d30b8) and again at the exit (0x1d3100) -- and the SECOND read decides Pop.  A handler that turns profiling off mid-frame gives a Push with no Pop (F2-j).  That is not an accident of code generation: the exit does not reuse the r3 the entry loaded.

F2 checks all three queues every frame and each handler returning goes to the NEXT check, not to the head: the order A -> B -> C is fixed and a frame runs each handler at most once (no loop edge anywhere in the 42 instructions).

the three queue cells are 12 B apart in one .bss cluster (0x542a4c / 0x542a58 / 0x542a64) but they are NOT the same object as the room: F3 clears list A's count behind UpdateActiveLists's back, so a frame that ran handler A leaves count A at 0 without F2 ever storing to it.
